feedback.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+3t \\ 2-4t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -4t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
